subject: math
title: Place Value
summary: Place value is the idea that the position of a digit in a number tells you its worth — the 5 in 573 means 500, but in 35 it means 5. Explore how hundreds, tens, and ones stack like blocks and why each position is worth ten times the one to its right.

compareCandidate.label: Place value vs. counting count-ups
compareCandidate.description: Place value encodes a number by (digit × place), so 35 is 3 tens and 5 ones. Counting just lists tally marks one by one with no positional meaning. Place value is why we can write huge numbers in only a few digits.

processes: Reading and writing numbers by place
Regrouping ten ones into one ten
plainLanguageExplanation: Place value means the value of a digit depends on where it sits in a number. Write 573 and read it as 5 hundreds + 7 tens + 3 ones. The 5 is worth 500 because it is in the hundreds place; a 5 could be just 5 if it sat in the ones place. This works because our number system is base ten — moving one position to the left multiplies a digit's value by ten, moving right divides by ten. Think of each number as a stack: tens are bundles of ten ones, hundreds are bundles of ten tens. When a column reaches ten it becomes a carry into the next place. Place value is the engine that lets a few symbols write any sized number.

keyFacts.label: Definition
keyFacts.value: A digit's value = its digit × its place (ones, tens, hundreds)

keyFacts.label: Base ten
keyFacts.value: Each place is 10× the place to its right

keyFacts.label: Regroup
keyFacts.value: Ten ones make one ten, ten tens make one hundred

keyFacts.label: More places
keyFacts.value: Thousands, ten-thousands, hundred-thousands continue the pattern

keyFacts.label: Worth
keyFacts.value: Position changes worth: 3 in 35 is 3, 3 in 350 is 30

whyItMatters: Place value is the doorway to all arithmetic. It lets us add by columns, borrow when subtracting, line up multiplication, understand big numbers, and later read decimals. Without identical place-shifts across the digits, standard paper-and-pencil math would not work, so this concept underpins many future skills.
tagline: A digit's position tells its worth
didYouKnow: Our place-value system is so efficient that with just ten digits you can write the number of sand grains on every beach — the position does all the heavy lifting.
compareReason: Place value decodes the digits hidden inside each number that a number line displays as a single point — together they show a number is both a position and a digit code.
